session.question: What tectonic processes are responsible for the formation of the Himalayan mountain range?
session.context:
pqac-5ebd8233: The excerpt is about fossil coryphoid palms from the K-Pg boundary in central India and their biogeographical implications. It discusses India’s docking with Eurasia in the early Paleogene and migration pathways after that collision, but it does not explain how the Himalayan mountain range formed. There is no direct information about tectonic processes such as plate collision, crustal shortening, or uplift of the Himalayas.
From Sanchita Kumar, Taposhi Hazra, Robert A. Spicer, Manoshi Hazra, Teresa E.V. Spicer, Subir Bera, and Mahasin Ali Khan. Coryphoid palms from the k-pg boundary of central india and their biogeographical implications: evidence from megafossil remains. Plant Diversity, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pld.2022.01.001, doi:10.1016/j.pld.2022.01.001.

pqac-e4262522: The excerpt is about fossil coryphoid palms from the K-Pg boundary in central India, their diversity, climate, and biogeographical history. It mentions that these fossils provide evidence for coryphoid palms in Gondwana prior to the India-Eurasia collision and trace migration after the Indian subcontinent docked with Eurasia early in the Paleogene. However, it does not discuss the tectonic processes responsible for forming the Himalayan mountain range.
From Sanchita Kumar, Taposhi Hazra, Robert A. Spicer, Manoshi Hazra, Teresa E.V. Spicer, Subir Bera, and Mahasin Ali Khan. Coryphoid palms from the k-pg boundary of central india and their biogeographical implications: evidence from megafossil remains. Plant Diversity, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pld.2022.01.001, doi:10.1016/j.pld.2022.01.001.
